NOTE: Nestle said in its annual report that the cost of raw materials -- particularly green coffee -- and of packaging materials decreased, but marketing expenditure rose to support new products and boost market share.
Distribution costs rose slightly as a percentage of sales, reflecting higher costs for ice cream and pet foods. Research and developmenet spending was unchanged in percentage terms.
Restructuring charges rose, but remained well below levels before 1995. Amortisation, representing an annual charge for all acquisitions made since January 1, 1995, also increased.
The trading margin was fractionally lower in Europe, mainly because of higher restructuring charges in western Europe. The profitability of eastern European operations increased.
Improvements in trading margins in North and South America reflected successful rationalisation programmes in the United States and Canada over recent years, it said.

In other regions, the decline in margins reflected costs linked to integrating acquisitions in the Australian ice cream and chilled dairy sectors. Margins improved in several emerging countries in Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
